articles.summary: New Ameriprise research explores how widowed adults are managing money, navigating financial decisions and finding support after loss For many widowed adults, managing finances independently wasn't a choice but an unexpected life transition. New research from Ameriprise Financial (NYSE: AMP) finds that many widowed Americans are moving forward with resilience despite facing one of life's most difficult transitions. Nearly nine in 10 (89%) feel financially confident, yet nearly six in 10 (58%) wish they had someone with whom they could share financial decisions. This desire for a financial sounding board highlights the value of having trusted support and guidance as widowed adults adapt to new responsibilities and make decisions about their future. The findings are part of Flying Solo: Navigating Financial Autonomy , an Ameriprise study examining how single, divorced and widowed Americans manage their finances. Widowed respondents made up 15% of the more than 3,000 solo adults
articles.title: Widowed Americans Are Financially Confident, Yet Many Miss a Trusted Financial Sounding Board
